subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy / logging constraints (FinLytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Hooper <andrew.hooper@finlytics.com>; Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finlytics.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy / logging constraints (FinLytics)

Hi Andrew / Marta,

Thanks again for the conversation today - this was really helpful to understand FinLytics' compliance needs. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned heading into the tech call.

Summary of pain / requirements (what I heard):
- PII leakage risk in inference logs (customer emails, account identifiers, occasionally free-text with SSNs) - must be removable or redacted on demand.
- Retention windows: customer-facing query logs = 30 days; operational/system logs = 365 days.
- Auditability: immutable audit trail for access/administration events and exportable JSON reports for security reviewers.
- Redaction: desire both edge pre-ingest redaction and server-side verification; ability to upload customer-specific regex rules.
- Data residency: some enterprise customers require EU-only processing for EU-origin data.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend: React dashboard used by analysts
- Backend: AWS (us-west-2) with S3 for raw logs and Redshift for analytics
- ML stack: in-house embeddings pipeline + occasional third-party API calls for generation
- Identity: Okta SSO / SCIM

Success criteria for pilot:
1) PII does not persist beyond specified retention windows and can be purged on request with verifiable audit trail
2) Redwood can be deployed in your VPC or provide strict region routing for EU customers
3) Audit logs produced meet your SOC2 checklist items for the initial vendor review
4) Embedding latency within 300ms p95 under test load

Proposed next steps:
- I'll attach a short SOC2 summary and a data-flow diagram that maps where logs are produced and stored (attached).
- Schedule a 60-min technical sync this week to scope the redaction/retention integration.
- If procurement needs docs early, I can share an NDA/SOW template after the tech call.

If anything above is off, please flag and I'll update. Otherwise I'll confirm the tech call slot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales (West) | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-soc2-2025-summary.pdf (stub), data-flow-diagram.png (stub)

From: Andrew Hooper <andrew.hooper@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy / logging constraints (FinLytics)

Marissa, thanks - this captures it well. A few clarifications from security/product: 

- Confirmed retention classes: Customer-facing queries (PII) = 30 days; Ops logs = 365 days. We may need deletions to be provable for audits.
- Redaction: we want pre-ingest edge redaction plus server-side verification. Can your API accept regex uploads per-customer?
- Audit exports: need JSON exports to our S3 bucket on a daily or weekly schedule.

Tech call availability: Wed 06/17 10:00 AM PT or Thu 06/18 2:00 PM PT. Please include your infra and privacy leads.

Marta - from security, do you want our vendor security spreadsheet completed before or after the infra sync?

Regards,
Andrew Hooper
Head of Product, FinLytics
andrew.hooper@finlytics.com | +1 206-555-9870

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Hooper <andrew.hooper@finlytics.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy / logging constraints (FinLytics)

Andrew - quick infra notes prior to the call: 

- Customer rules: Redwood supports per-customer rule sets on the request router. Rules can be uploaded via API or configured in the Console. We support regex redaction and an ML-based PII detector for names/emails/credit-cards.
- Retention: configurable per-log-type retention policies (30d / 365d). Deletion actions create a tombstone record and an immutable audit event that we can export.
- Exports: JSON audit exports to customer S3 buckets are supported; we can schedule daily snapshots.
- Deployment: Pilot can run as Redwood Private in your AWS account (VPC) or Hosted with region pinning for US-only traffic.

I'll prepare sample API payloads for rule upload, an example retention-config file, and a short demo of the redaction pipeline for the tech call.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks all - confirming the tech call for Wed 2026-06-17 10:00 AM PT. Calendar invite sent - agenda below: 

Agenda (45m):
- 10m: Introductions & scope (Marissa / Andrew)
- 15m: Infra run-through (Dev) - ingestion points, logging locations, redaction flow
- 15m: Compliance & retention (Stephanie) - deletion workflow, audit exports, proof for SOC2
- 5m: Next steps / pilot timeline

Prep items for FinLytics:
- A sample of redacted logs and list of PII types to treat specially (emails, account IDs, SSNs).
- Any regex rules you already use.
- Vendor security spreadsheet if you want us to pre-populate it before review.

I've attached the SOC2 summary, data-flow diagram, and a stub PCI/PSM doc we sometimes share with finance customers. I'll follow up with an SOW template after the tech call if procurement wants an early look.

Cheers,
Marissa
